questions.question: Name four common causes of fires in homes or in the veld.
questions.expected_answer: Any four: paraffin stoves or heaters knocked over or filled while burning; candles left burning near curtains or while sleeping; open fires or braziers left unattended; children playing with matches or lighters; faulty wiring, overloaded multiplugs or illegal connections; cooking oil left on the stove; burning rubbish or careless cigarettes in dry, windy veld.

questions.question: Give four rules for preventing fires at home.
questions.expected_answer: Any four: stand stoves on a firm, flat surface away from curtains and bedding; never fill a paraffin stove while it is burning; put candles in a stable holder like a tin of sand and never leave them burning unattended; keep matches and lighters out of reach of young children; never leave cooking unattended; store paraffin in labelled, child-proof containers; do not overload multiplugs; fit a smoke alarm.

questions.question: What should you do if there is a fire in your home, and if your clothes catch fire?
questions.expected_answer: Shout Fire, get everyone out quickly, crawl low under smoke, feel doors before opening them, never go back inside, meet at a safe place and call 10177 or 112. If your clothes catch fire, stop, drop to the ground, cover your face and roll to smother the flames.
